Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:10:1.hebrew: לכדר' ינאי - להכי כתב "גם" לרבויי שליח, משום דבעי לאקושי למשלחו, למימר דבעובד כוכבים פסול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:10:1.english: For that [statement] of Rabbi Yannai - It is for this [reason that the verse] wrote “also” to include an agent: because it needed to juxtapose [the agent] to the one who sent him, to state that regarding a gentile, [he is] disqualified.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:11:1.hebrew: לפי שאינו כו' - אלמא לא בעי קרא, דמסברא אית לן למימר, דמידי דלא שייך ביה — לא מתעביד עליה שליח:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:11:1.english: Because he is not, etc. - Consequently, a verse is not required, as by logical reasoning we can say that regarding a matter that does not apply to him, he cannot be made an agent concerning it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:12:1.hebrew: לאו בר היתירא הוא גרסי' - אינו בשום צד היתר אשת איש, שאינו מגרש, דהא אין לו קידושין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:12:1.english: "He is not subject to release" is our reading - He is not in any respect [part of] the permitting of a married woman, for he cannot divorce, since he has no [capacity for] betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:12:3.hebrew: תרומתן תרומה - ליאסר לזרים, דקסבר: אין קנין לעובד כוכבים בארץ ישראל להפקיע, ומירוח עובד כוכבים אינו פוטר מן התרומה. ובמנחות (דף סז.) יליף לה טעמא מדגנך דגנך תרי זימני, למעוטי דיגון עובד כוכבים, ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:12:3.english: Their teruma is teruma - [In that it takes effect] to be forbidden to non-priests, for he holds: Acquisition [of land] by a gentile in the Land of Israel does not have the power to abrogate [the obligation of tithes], and smoothing [the pile] by a gentile does not exempt [the produce] from teruma. And in Menachot (daf 67a), [the Gemara] derives the reason for this from "your grain" [and] "your grain" two times, to exclude grain-piling by a gentile; and an exclusion following an exclusion serves only to include.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:1.english: Renders [produce] a mixture - If it falls into non-sacred produce, it renders it forbidden.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:2.english: And [one] is liable to [pay] an added fifth for it - [This refers to] one who eats it unwittingly.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:3.hebrew: ור' שמעון פוטר - דקסבר: אין מירוח העובד כוכבים חייב בתרומה, ויליף לה מדגנך — ולא דיגון עובד כוכבים — במנחות (שם). ולדידיה, ליכא מיעוט אחר מיעוט, דמצריך להו צריכי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:3.english: And Rabbi Shimon exempts - For he holds that the smoothing [of the grain pile] of a gentile is not obligated in teruma, and he derives this from “your grain” — and not the grain-piling of a gentile — in Menachot (ibid.). And according to him, there is no exclusion following an exclusion, for he requires them [all] as necessary [for distinct derivations].

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:4.hebrew: אתם גם אתם למה לי - פשיטא דלא הוי עובד כוכבים שליח, דהא ליתיה בתרומה דנפשיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:13:4.english: “You,” “you also,” why do I need [them]? - It is obvious that a gentile cannot be an agent, for he is not [included] in teruma of his own.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:14:1.hebrew: איצטריך - לרבויי שליח לתרומה. משום דכתיב "אתם" למעוטי אריסים מלתרום חלקו של בעה"ב, ואפטרופוס יתומים, והתורם את שאינו שלו שלא מדעתו — אימא למעוטי נמי שליח; להכי איצטריך "גם" לרבויי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:14:1.english: It was necessary - To include an agent for [separating] teruma. For since it is written “you” to exclude sharecroppers from separating [teruma from] the landowner’s portion, and a guardian of orphans, and one who separates that which is not his without [the owner's] consent — I might say [that it comes] to exclude an agent as well; therefore, “also” was necessary to include [an agent].

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:15:1.english: This works out well according to Rabbi Yehoshua - For he derives [the principle of] agency for sacrificial offerings from “and they shall slaughter it.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:1:1.english: [If] he subtracted ten - That he separated one-fortieth.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:1:2.english: His teruma is teruma - For [the agent] says to him: “This is how I estimated you.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:1:3.english: From where do we [derive this] - That an agent [may] separate teruma.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:1:4.hebrew: גם אתם - כן תרימו גם אתם, והאי גם יתירא הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:1:4.english: You also - [The verse states:] “So you also shall set apart,” and this [word] “also” is superfluous.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:2:1.hebrew: במחשבה - נותן עיניו בצד זה, ואוכל בצד זה, דכתיב (במדבר יח) ונחשב:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:2:1.english: By thought - One sets his eyes on this side [to designate it as teruma], and eats on that side, as it is written (Numbers 18): “And it shall be reckoned.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:3:1.english: And they said to one - [One] of the members of their group.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:3:2.english: Go and search - [For] the lost Paschal offering.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:3:3.hebrew: והן אוכלין עמו - שהרי עשאוהו שליח לשחוט, ושלהן פסול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:3:3.english: And they eat with him - For they made him an agent to slaughter [on their behalf], and their [offering] is disqualified.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:4:1.english: From where do we [derive this] - That a person's agent is like himself for the slaughter of sacrificial offerings.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:4:2.hebrew: אצל קדשים - אפי' תרומה חול הוא אצלו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:4:2.english: Relative to offerings - Even teruma is [considered] non-sacred relative to it.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:6:1.hebrew: רוב מעשיהם - כל עבודת הקרבתם ע"י כהנים, שהם שלוחים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:6:1.english: The majority of their actions - All the service of offering them [is performed] by means of priests, who are agents.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:7:1.english: Which [one] will be derived - This is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:8:1.hebrew: שכן ישנן במחשבה - קדשים נמי איתנהו במחשבה (וכן נמי פסול קדשים ופיגול ע"י מחשבה הם באים) — גמר בלבו לומר: "שור זה עולה" — הרי הוא עולה, כדתני' בשבועות בפ"ג (דף כו:): "מוצא שפתיך" — אין לי אלא שהוציא בשפתיו; גמר בלבו מנין? ת"ל: "כל נדיב לב עולות":
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:8:1.english: For they can be [effected] by thought - Sacrificial offerings are also [effective] through thought (and so too, the disqualification of sacrificial offerings and piggul come about through thought) — [if] one determined in his heart to say: "This ox is a burnt-offering," it is a burnt-offering, as it is taught in Shevuot in chapter 3 (daf 26b): "'That which is gone out of your lips' — I have [derived] only [a case] where he expressed [it] with his lips; from where [do I derive that it is binding if] he determined in his heart? The verse states: 'All who are of a willing heart [brought] burnt-offerings.'"

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:9:1.hebrew: ותיתי מהנך - מה קדשים שהן קדש ישנן בשליח, תרומה שהיא חול — לא כל שכן? מה לקדשים, שכן רוב מעשיהם ע"י שליח? גירושין יוכיחו. מה לגירושין, שכן ישנן חול אצל תרומה? קדשים יוכיחו. וחזר הדין: הצד השוה שבהן — שישנן ע"י עצמו ושלוחו כמותו, אף אני אביא תרומה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:9:1.english: And let it be derived from these - Just as [with] offerings, which are sacred, they can be [effected] through an agent, [with regard to] terumah, which is non-sacred [relative to them], is it not all the more so? What [can be objected] regarding offerings? That most of their actions are [performed] through an agent. Divorce will prove [otherwise]. What [can be objected] regarding divorce? That it is non-sacred relative to terumah. Offerings will prove [otherwise]. And the derivation revolves: The common denominator between them is that they can be [performed] by oneself, and [yet] one's agent is like oneself; so too, I will include terumah [that one's agent is like oneself].

Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:9:2.hebrew: ה"ג - אבל עובד כוכבים, הואיל ואיתיה בתרומה דנפשיה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 41b:9:2.english: This is the text we read - “But a gentile, since he is included in his own teruma.”

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:12:1.hebrew: העובד כוכבים והכותי שתרמו תרומתן תרומה - פירש הקונט': ליאסר לזרים, דקסבר אין קנין לעובד כוכבים בארץ ישראל להפקיע, ומירוח העובד כוכבים אינו פוטר מן התרומה. ובמנחות (דף סז.) יליף טעמא מדגנך, "דגנך" תרי זימני: למעוטי דיגון עובד כוכבים, ואין מיעוט אחר מיעוט אלא לרבות — מדמעת, אם נפלה בחולין אוסרתה, וחייבין עליה חומש האוכלה בשוגג. ור"ש פוטר, דקסבר אין מירוח העובד כוכבים חייב בתרומה, ויליף: "מדגנך" — ולא דיגון עובד כוכבים; ולדידיה ליכא מיעוט אחר מיעוט, דמצריך להו אצרוכי, עכ"ל. וקשה לפי', דמשמע דפליגי ביש קנין לעובד כוכבים, ובפ' השולח (גיטין מז.) פליגי בה אמוראי, ואין סברא לומר דפליגי תנאי בפלוגתא דאמוראי. לכך פי' ר"י, דת"ק סבר דאפי' יש קנין משכחת שפיר שתבואתו חייב בתרומה, כגון שגדלה שליש בידי ישראל. ואי משום מירוח העובד כוכבים דפוטר — י"ל דמיירי שמרחו ישראל. ואי משום "זרעך" ולא לקוח — י"ל דמיירי שלקחם קודם מירוח ואח"כ מירחם ישראל, ופטורא דלקוח אינו אלא אחר מירוח; כן פי' ר"ת. וקשה, דא"כ דומיא דהכי פוטר ר"ש, ומאי טעמא? וי"ל דטעמא כדאמר [בזבחים] (דף מה.), דאמר ר"ש: קדשי עובדי כוכבים אין בהם מעילה, משום דילפינן "חטא" "חטא" מתרומה, ובתרומה כתיב "בני ישראל" ולא עובדי כוכבים — אלמא ממעט ליה מקרא בהדיא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:12:1.english: "A gentile and a Samaritan who separated teruma, their teruma is teruma" - The Kuntres explained: [It is considered teruma] to become forbidden to non-priests, for he holds that a gentile does not have [the power of] acquisition in the Land of Israel to uproot [the obligation of tithes], and smoothing [the grain pile] by a gentile does not exempt [the produce] from teruma. And in Menachot (67a), [the Gemara] derives the reason from [the repetition of] "your grain" [and] "your grain" two times: to exclude the grain piling of a gentile; and a limitation after a limitation serves only to amplify — [meaning that this produce] causes a mixture (medama), [so that] if it falls into non-sacred produce (chullin) it renders it forbidden, and one who eats it inadvertently is liable to pay an [additional] fifth. And Rabbi Shimon exempts [it], for he holds that the smoothing of a gentile is not obligated in teruma, and he derives [this from]: "Your grain" — and not the grain piling of a gentile; and according to him, there is no limitation after a limitation, because he requires them [the occurrences of "your grain"] for [distinct] necessary derivations. Until here are his [Rashi's] words. And this is difficult according to his explanation: For it implies that they disagree over whether a gentile has [the power of] acquisition [in the Land of Israel to uproot tithes], whereas in the chapter [entitled] HaShole'ach (Gittin 47a), Amora'im disagree about this, and it is not reasonable to say that Tanna'im disagree in a dispute of Amora'im. Therefore, the Ri explained that the First Tanna holds that even if [a gentile] has [the power of] acquisition, you can well find that his produce is obligated in teruma, such as where it reached a third of its growth in the possession of an Israelite. And if [you object] because smoothing by a gentile exempts [produce from teruma] — one can say that it is dealing with a case where an Israelite smoothed it. And if [you object] because of [the verse]: "[the increase of] your seed" — and not purchased produce — one can say that it is dealing with a case where he purchased them before smoothing and afterward an Israelite smoothed them, and the exemption of purchased produce applies only after smoothing; so explained Rabbeinu Tam. And it is difficult: For if so, in a similar case Rabbi Shimon exempts, and what is the reason? And one can say that the reason is as [the Gemara] states [in Zevachim] (45a), where Rabbi Shimon says: Sacrificial items of gentiles are not subject to [the laws of] misuse (me'ila), because we derive [by verbal analogy] "sin" [from] "sin" from teruma, and regarding teruma it is written: "the children of Israel" — and not gentiles; evidently, Scripture explicitly excludes them.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:1:1.hebrew: פיחת י' או הוסיף י' תרומתו תרומה - פי' בקונטרס: פיחת — שתרם א' ממ', וקאי פיחת אבעל הבית. וי"מ איפכא: דפיחת — שתרם אחד מששים, וקאי פיחת אתרומה. מ"מ משמע: היכא דתרם השליח, ואפי' אתא בעה"ב ואמר לו: "לא היה בדעתי לכך" — אפ"ה תרומתו תרומה. וקשה: דמאי שנא מדהא דאמר (ב"מ דף כב.): "האומר לשלוחו: 'צא ותרום', והלך ותרם; אם א"ל בעה"ב: 'כלך אצל יפות' — אם נמצאו יפות מהן תרומתו תרומה, ואם לאו אין תרומתו תרומה"? ומוקי לה התם: כגון דשויה בעה"ב שליח, ואפ"ה אין תרומתו תרומה, כיון שלא פירש לו בהדיא שמתרצה ליפות! וי"ל: דהתם היינו טעמא — לפי שאין דרך בני אדם לברור היפות כדי לתרום אלא הבינונים; אבל הכא, דיש הרבה בני אדם דדרכן לתרום בעין יפה, מצי למימר ליה: "להכי אמדתיך, ובטלת דעתך אצל דעתי למה שאמדתיך":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:1:1.english: [If] he subtracted ten or added ten, his teruma is teruma - Rashi explained in the Kuntres: "He subtracted" — that he separated one-fortieth, and "he subtracted" refers to the owner. And some explain the opposite: that "he subtracted" — that he separated one-sixtieth, and "he subtracted" refers to the teruma. In any case, it implies: Wherever the agent separated [the] teruma, and even if the owner came and said to him: "It was not my intention [to do] so" — even so, his teruma is teruma. And [this] is difficult: For how is [this] different from that which [the Gemara] said (Bava Metzia 22a): "One who says to his agent: 'Go out and separate teruma,' and he went and separated [it] — if the owner said to him: 'Go to the choice [produce],' if [produce] better than them was found, his teruma is teruma; and if not, his teruma is not teruma"? And [the Gemara] establishes it there [as a case] where the owner made him an agent, and even so his teruma is not teruma, since he did not explicitly state to him that he consents to the choice [produce]! And one can say: There, this is the reason — because it is not the practice of people to select the choice [produce] in order to separate [it as] teruma, but rather the intermediate [produce]; but here, since there are many people whose practice is to separate [it] with a generous eye, [the agent] can say to him: "I estimated you for this, and your intention is nullified in relation to my intention regarding that which I estimated you."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:1:2.hebrew: מה לגירושין שכן ישנן חול - אבל לא מצי למימר: "שכן ישנן בע"כ", כי ההיא דלעיל — דאיכא למימר: קידושין יוכיחו. אבל לעיל לא מייתי ליה אלא גבי קידושין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:1:2.english: What [is unique] to divorce is that it is non-sacred - However, [the Gemara] could not say: "[What is unique to divorce is] that it can be [effected] against her will," like that [challenge] above, because one could say: Let betrothal prove [otherwise]. However, above, [the Gemara] only brought it [this challenge] with regard to betrothal.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:2:1.hebrew: שכן ישנה במחשבה - ומיהו קידושין הוו אתו מתרומה ומגירושין; דכי פרכת: מה לגירושין שכן ישנן בע"כ — תרומה תוכיח, מה לתרומה שכן ישנה במחשבה — גירושין יוכיחו. ומיהו מהיקישא דויצאה והיתה לא הוה מצי מפיק, דאיצטריך לשאר דרשות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:2:1.english: "In that it is [effected] by thought" - And nevertheless, betrothal could have been derived from teruma and from divorce; for if you were to object: "What [is unique] about divorce is that it can be [effected] against her will" — teruma would prove [otherwise]; [and if you were to object:] "What [is unique] about teruma is that it can be [effected] by thought" — divorce would prove [otherwise]. And nevertheless, from the juxtaposition [hekkesh] of "and she departs and becomes" one could not have derived [it], as it was needed for other expositions.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:5:1.hebrew: נפקא ליה מדר' יהושע בן קרחה - וא"ת: אמאי לא יליף דשליחות מהני בקדשים משחיטת פרו של אהרן, מדאיצטריך לומר שהיה בבעלים, כדכתיב (ויקרא ט״ז:י״א): "ושחט את פר החטאת אשר לו" — מכלל דבשאר קדשים לא בעינן בעלים? וי"ל: דהא דממעטינן מפרו של אהרן, היינו חטאת דווקא, דומיא דפרו של אהרן; וה"ט: משום דבחטאת כתיב "אותו" — אפי' בע"כ, והלכך, כיון דאי איתא לקמן מקריבין אותו בע"כ, דין הוא שיעשה שליח; אבל שאר קרבנות, דלא מקריבין בע"כ, לא הוה ידעינן שיכול לעשות שליח, אי לא דנפקא ליה מדר' יהושע בן קרחה:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:5:1.english: He derives it from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa - And if you say: Why does the Gemara not derive that agency is effective regarding sacrificial offerings from the slaughter of Aaron’s bull, from the fact that it was necessary to state that it had to be performed by the owner, as it is written (Leviticus 16:11): “And he shall slaughter the bull of the sin-offering which is his” — which implies that for other sacrificial offerings we do not require the owner himself? And one can say: That which we exclude from Aaron’s bull is specifically a sin-offering, similar to Aaron’s bull; and this is the reason: because regarding a sin-offering it is written “it” — even against his will. And therefore, since as it is stated below, they sacrifice it against his will, it is logical that he may appoint an agent; but regarding other sacrifices, which they do not sacrifice against his will, we would not have known that he can appoint an agent, were it not that he derives it from Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:8:1.hebrew: שכן ישנן במחשבה - תרומה — דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:כ״ז): "ונחשב לכם תרומתכם"; וקדשים — דכתיב בדברי הימים (ב כט): "כל נדיב לב עולות":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 41b:8:1.english: "For they can be [designated] by means of thought" - Teruma — as it is written (Numbers 18:27): "And your teruma shall be reckoned to you"; and consecrated offerings — as it is written in Chronicles (II 29:31): "all who were of a willing heart [brought] burnt-offerings."
